tower-of-hanoi.title: Place largest disk on target first
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When the goal is to assemble the full tower on a specific peg, move the largest disk onto that peg before any smaller disks are placed there. This guarantees that the largest disk forms the base and avoids later size violations.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Goal is to have all disks on one peg and the largest disk is not already there.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to place disk 4 onto the target peg before moving disk 5, which later blocks disk 5 from being placed correctly.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive Hanoi move sequence
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move a stack of n disks from a source peg to a target peg using an auxiliary peg, first recursively move the top n‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, then move the largest disk, and finally move the n‑1 disks from the auxiliary peg onto the target. This classic recursion respects all size constraints.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: You need to transfer a contiguous stack of disks from one peg to another.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving the largest disk directly from source to target without first moving the smaller disks to the auxiliary peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate each move's legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before committing a move, check that the chosen disk is the topmost on its source peg and that the destination peg’s top disk (if any) is larger than the moving disk. This prevents illegal moves such as moving a non‑top disk or placing a larger disk onto a smaller one.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Every time you generate a move.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 3 from a peg where disk 1 is on top, violating the top‑disk rule.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear blocking disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the disk you need to move has smaller disks stacked on top, relocate those smaller disks to other pegs first. Only after the larger disk is exposed can it be moved safely.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the desired disk is not the topmost on its peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move disk 5 while disks 2 and 1 remain stacked on top of it.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use smallest disk as temporary buffer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be placed on any peg without violating size rules, making it ideal for temporary buffering while larger disks are repositioned.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need a free peg to move larger disks and the smallest disk is available.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Neglecting to move the smallest disk out of the way, causing a deadlock when larger disks need a free peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Build target stack from largest to smallest
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When constructing the final tower on the goal peg, place disks in descending size order, starting with the largest and working down to the smallest. This ensures the final ordering is correct.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When assembling the final tower on the goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing disk 2 onto the target peg before disk 3, resulting in an incorrect order.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear target blocking disk before moving larger disk onto it
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the destination peg has a smaller disk on top, move that disk elsewhere before attempting to place a larger disk onto the peg. This clears the target so the size rule is not violated.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before moving a larger disk onto a peg that already contains disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 4 onto a peg where disk 2 is on top, violating the size ordering.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat existing larger disks on target as base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the target peg already holds some of the final stack’s larger disks in the correct order, treat them as a fixed base and only move the remaining smaller disks onto them.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the goal peg already contains correctly ordered larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 5 onto a peg that already contains disk 4 but not in the required bottom‑up order, ignoring the existing correct base.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may treat the move list as optional or simply forget to generate it after reasoning.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always generate a non‑empty list of moves before finishing the answer; explicitly write the list even if it is long.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (size ordering violation)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model focuses on moving the correct disk but neglects to check the destination peg’s top disk size.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before each move, compare the moving disk’s size with the top disk on the destination peg; only move onto an empty peg or onto a larger disk.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a non‑top disk (attempting to move a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model selects a disk based on the goal without verifying its current position on the peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Check that the chosen disk is the topmost on its source peg before issuing the move.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The generated move sequence exceeds the response length limit, causing the tail of the list to be cut off.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Keep the move sequence concise (e.g., by using the recursive algorithm) or ensure the entire list fits within the allowed token budget before finalizing the answer.
